opportunities.title: Golden cases for the creative critic: does it catch a degraded film?
opportunities.why: The chain's tests walk fixture artefacts and do not show that any agent's judgement is good. The critic is the last line before the user; nothing measures whether it ranks a deliberately degraded cut below its source.
definitionOfDone: Build at least six pairs of a reference and a copy degraded on one axis with ref:degrade (timing, hierarchy, sync, frozen tint), from material you may share.
Run the critic on each with your own Claude Code or Codex session (no paid provider APIs) and record its critiques as fixtures.
Add an offline scorer and a test that reports, per axis, how often the degraded copy scored lower; publish the rate in docs/craft-evaluation.md with the model and harness used.

value.rationale: The critic is the last judge before the user; a measured detection rate per degradation axis shows whether its verdicts can be trusted.

opportunities.title: Measure position bias in the creative director's pairwise judging
opportunities.why: The creative director judges every pair in both orders, but nothing reports how often the winner flips with the order, so a judge that prefers whatever it sees first goes unnoticed.
definitionOfDone: Add a pure function over recorded pairwise entries that reports the order-flip rate and the first-shown win rate.
Surface both numbers in the review artefact and warn above a stated threshold; test the boundary with fixtures.
Document the reading in docs/production-chain.md.

value.rationale: A judge that prefers whatever it sees first corrupts every idea and script ranking; the flip rate makes that bias visible.

opportunities.title: Does the creative rubric predict what people prefer?
opportunities.why: Ideas and scripts are ranked on a frozen rubric, but no evidence ties its scores to human preference; the benchmark guide says so.
definitionOfDone: Propose a protocol (RFC draft under docs/rfcs/): blind human preference pairs on benchmark outputs, sample size and agreement statistic with an interval.
After design approval, implement the offline analysis with fixtures and publish the first result with its uncertainty.

value.rationale: The frozen rubric ranks every idea and script; without evidence that it tracks human preference, the ranking may optimise the wrong thing.

opportunities.title: Fence untrusted film and web text in agent briefs
opportunities.why: The category scout reads web pages and the reference analyst reads other people's films, including their on-screen and spoken words. Neither brief marks that material as data, so an injected instruction in a page or a caption reaches the agent as plain text.
definitionOfDone: Wrap external text that briefs pass to agents in clearly delimited, labelled blocks and state in the two agent files that such text is data, never instructions.
Add a test with an injected instruction in a reference's speech text and a scraped page, asserting it only appears inside the fence.
Report the change through the security process first if you find an exploitable path.

value.rationale: Closes a prompt-injection path from scraped pages and other people's films into agent briefs.

opportunities.title: Contract fixtures for the voiceover agents
opportunities.why: No test names caption-editor, narrator-director or voice-producer, so a prompt edit can silently break the artefact each one must write.
definitionOfDone: For each agent, add a realistic example of the artefact it writes under tests/fixtures/ and validate it with the Zod schema the next stage reads.
Assert that every artefact path and field the agent file promises exists in that schema.
Split into several S pull requests if you prefer, one agent each.

value.rationale: Catches a prompt edit that silently breaks the artefact a voiceover agent must write, before a user's project does.

opportunities.title: What breaks on smaller models? A measured run
opportunities.why: The README says taste depends on the model and that smaller models follow rules but judge less well; nobody has measured where they fail.
definitionOfDone: Run the benchmark suite's offline tasks with a smaller model on your own harness, without paid provider calls, and submit signed bundles.
Write which steps failed, with evidence, and propose rule or tool changes that make a smaller model safer.

value.rationale: Shows where smaller models fail the studio's rules, so rules and tools can make them safer; bundles must be signed to count.

opportunities.title: Measured music-fit evidence for agents that cannot hear
opportunities.why: Agents read loudness, beats and spectra but cannot judge whether a track fits; a measured comparison of the cut's structure with the music's would give the user better evidence before they listen.
definitionOfDone: Add an offline reading that compares cut density and section changes with the track's energy and section map, using the existing audio analysis.
Report it as evidence, never as a verdict on taste; test it on synthetic fixtures with known alignment.

value.rationale: Agents cannot hear; measured agreement between the cut and the music's structure gives the user evidence before they listen.

opportunities.title: Cover lyric videos
opportunities.why: "Lyric video for my song" only weakly matches motion-design; timed lyrics, licensing of the user's own track and caption styling are not part of any method.
evidence: pnpm playbook --match "lyric video for my song"
definitionOfDone: Decide with evidence between a variant of motion-design and a new playbook; run pnpm contrib:novelty.
Add match regressions for English and Russian requests and checkable intake and QA lines.

value.rationale: A common request with no clear route today; a stated method sets its intake, rights and QA.

opportunities.title: Cover recipe and cooking videos
opportunities.why: "Recipe cooking video" matches no playbook today, although step-by-step food content is a large short-form format.
definitionOfDone: Decide whether it is footage-edit, product-tutorial or a new playbook; run pnpm contrib:novelty.
Add match regressions, intake questions about the user's own footage and QA lines for readable steps and quantities.

value.rationale: A large short-form format that matches no playbook today.

opportunities.title: Route podcast audiograms
opportunities.why: "Podcast audiogram" falls to footage-edit, which expects video; an audio-only episode with a waveform and captions has no stated route.
definitionOfDone: Add the request to the right playbook's triggers or a variant, with a match regression and the blocks it would use.

value.rationale: Audio-only episodes fall to a playbook that expects video; a stated route avoids a wrong method.

opportunities.title: Analyse reference films for genres with none
opportunities.why: The reference corpus has 22 analysed films, mostly product and motion films; genres such as UGC ads, event recaps and case studies have no measured reference to learn from.
definitionOfDone: Analyse a film you may study with ref:add and ref:analyze, then contribute its structure-only layers with ref:contribute.
Link the techniques it confirms to technique cards; never commit frames, media or verbatim text.

value.rationale: Measured references are what agents learn editing from; uncovered genres have none. Only films you have the rights to study qualify, and only structure-only layers are contributed.

opportunities.title: Make one of the first showcase films, on the free route
opportunities.why: The gallery is empty. A film rendered locally from library blocks, with no paid calls, shows newcomers what the studio does and proves the free route.
definitionOfDone: Make a film with your own harness without paid provider calls, keep its pipeline artefacts and submit it as a showcase entry with rights and licence declared.

value.rationale: The empty gallery is the first thing a newcomer sees; one locally rendered film proves the free route. You must hold the rights to every material and declare them.
